Subject: TitanBank deal — feature tradeoffs & temporary scope ask

Hi team,

Quick context: TitanBank (large commercial banking account) is at procurement sign-off but we hit a gating ask — they want a small set of audit/traceability features and a tenant-level export capability delivered before contract signature (they've tied pricing to a go-live milestone). Procurement gave a firm target: signed PO by 2027-05-12, pilot in production week of 2027-05-24.

Attachments: titanbank_mvp_requirements.pdf, titanbank_procurement_timeline.xlsx

What I'm asking from Product/Eng: can we propose a pragmatic, short-lived implementation plan that gets TitanBank the audit export and a scoped traceability view within ~2-3 weeks? If full product work is large, please propose a temporary shim/guardrail we can ship behind a feature flag (customer opt-in) or a manual export process that Engineering can support for one quarter while Product scopes the long-term solution.

Deal economics: ACV target $480k ARR; expansion motion likely if we meet the pilot. Legal and Procurement are already pushing on timeline. If we miss this cadence, procurement will escalate for concessions.

Key questions (need answers by EOD Monday 2027-05-09):
- High-level feasibility: can Eng deliver an export + basic traceability UI (read-only) behind a flag in 2–3 weeks?
- Minimal scope list: what is the smallest set we can ship that satisfies their procurement checklist?
- Risk and operational burden: what manual work will be required from SRE/Support for the pilot?
- Temporary mitigations: are there acceptable fallbacks (manual CSV export + one-off log retention policy) we can commit to?

I flagged Markus because we need product sign-off on the acceptable tradeoffs; Dev to confirm engineering ETA and ops load. Grace/Rishi — I know you'll want to align on contract language and go/no-go.

Appreciate a short reply per question above; we can spin a quick 20-30m sync Tue if helpful.

Thanks —

Naomi — thanks for the clear brief and attachments. I skimmed the PDF; the procurement checklist calls out:
- Tenant-level export of audit events for queries and completions (CSV, S3 delivery ok)
- Traceability view that maps request IDs to the model variant, timestamp, and routing decision
- Retention proof: 90 days for pilot, with option to extend

High-level take: we can likely do a scoped delivery if we accept a temporary, best-effort implementation that is explicitly labeled as an "enterprise pilot capability (limited support)."

But I need answers on two product/design decisions before committing:
1) Export format: Is CSV + S3 push acceptable for their compliance team (simpler) or do they insist on a UI-driven export?
2) Access model: should the exported dataset contain PII-filtered payloads or full message content? (legal will want to avoid full raw content unless contract controls are explicit)

If CSV+S3 + PII-filtered is acceptable, Dev and I can scope a prototype: backend export job + small admin UI to trigger and monitor. Tentative estimate: 10–12 eng days (Dev + one engineer), delivery in ~2 calendar weeks if started Mon 2027-05-10. That assumes we can schedule a small SRE window for one-off export jobs and set a temporary retention policy.

I'll block time for a short sync Tue 2027-05-11 to confirm scope.

— Markus

Markus/Naomi — quick engineering read: the backend already logs enough metadata to assemble the requested traceability mapping (request_id -> model_variant -> route -> timestamp). The gap is a supported export pipeline and a minimal admin surface.

Options and rough effort (minimal viable paths):
A) CSV+S3 export job (scripted) + admin button to trigger exports (no fancy UI): ~8 eng days (Dev + 1). Requires SRE window to approve elevated job access for the pilot.
B) Small UI + scheduled exports + basic parsing/filter pipeline for PII: ~12 eng days. Adds ~2 days of ops to configure retention policies.
C) Manual support fallback: we can run one-off exports and hand over CSVs to TitanBank for initial procurement sign-off — 1–3 eng-days of ad-hoc ops every time (not sustainable beyond pilot).

Constraints:
- We don't currently have an automated PII-filter that matches major banks' definitions; the simplest approach is to redact payload text columns and surface only metadata for the pilot (request id, model id, timestamp, route). That will likely satisfy audit teams in many cases but we should validate with TitanBank security.
- If they demand raw transcripts, legal will need to sign off and we should propose a data escrow pattern.

I can start on Option A on Mon 2027-05-10 if Product confirms scope.

— Dev
